newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Dollar limbers up for push to 1.70 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar limbers up for push to 1.70 marks.

text.p: The dollar is knocking on the door of an upchannel around 1.6940 marks, looking for an opening to key trendline resistance at 1.70, chart watchers said.

"Prices are finding resistance at the upband in the 1.6940 area, but if they succeed in taking that out they can easily break through the level just above 1.70," said Geert-Jan Nikken, technical analyst at ABN AMRO in Amsterdam.
Failure to breach 1.70 would leave the dollar in a potential head-and-shoulders formation on daily charts, some said.
The dollar was trading at 1.6938/45 marks at 0716 GMT versus 1.6897/02 in late Europe on Monday.

"The spike down to 1.6780 completed the short-term correction, clearing the way for renewed strength to 1.7010 and eventually 1.7300-80," said Eddie Matts, director at Capital Management UK. Reactions should now hold 1.6840, he added.
Analysts placed immediate support around 1.6875, a congestion zone and prop from the dollar's retracement of its decline from the 1.7120 marks high hit on May 20.

Chartists' favoured scenario for dollar/mark is bullish, however -- and the same applies for dollar/yen. That pair is now seen gearing up for a push through 117, though dips should hold the 116.00-115.80 region, analysts said.
Beneath there, the 115.50/30 congestion area should keep dollar/yen in consolidative mode, analysts said.
The dollar was quoted at 116.02/12 yen at 0732 GMT versus 116.44/49 in late Europe yesterday.
Ahead of the 117 area, interim resistance cuts in around 116.65, said Nikken at ABN AMRO.
That represents an extension target set by the breakout from a consolidation triangle on hourly charts, as well as the overnight Asian high, he explained.
